body:
VERDICT: Record A applies. The observation cursor of the integration represented by this workspace is GLOBAL — one durable, filter-independent position in the store's single commit order. Record B's "per-consumer, independent position" does not describe the current pinned line.

INTEGRATION / "CURRENT PINNED LINE"
The workspace is Palimpsest (`palimpsest-dsh`) consuming Ordarium via GitHub release tarballs. The current pinned line is Ordarium v1.3.1, fixed by three independent places that agree:
- package.json:32-37 (@ordarium/core|host-kit|ledger-sqlite at ordarium-v1.3.1 tarballs; testing as devDep);
- pnpm-workspace.yaml:15-18 (the load-bearing overrides, same four 1.3.1 URLs);
- the installed artifacts: node_modules/@ordarium/core/package.json and node_modules/@ordarium/ledger-sqlite/package.json both report "version": "1.3.1".
Note the archive prose is stale relative to the pin: 07-ordarium-alignment.md's last revision (r19, 2026-09-07) records a 1.2.0 pin and declares the executable backlog cleared, and test/ordarium_ledger.test.ts still expects ledger user_version 3 whereas 1.3.1 ships schema v4 (LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION = 4). Therefore "current pinned line" must be read from the manifest plus the installed artifacts, not from the archive's narrative.

WHICH CURSOR "OBSERVATION" DENOTES
In the pinned line the only cursor Ordarium calls observation is the ORD-BOOT-0 state change feed — OrdariumStateStore.changes / StateChangeFeed — documented as "Incremental observation of committed state revisions after a durable position" (core/dist/src/state.d.ts; core/dist/src/types.d.ts:182-190). No other Ordarium surface (host-kit included) uses "observation" or defines a cursor contract.

WHAT THE PINNED ARTIFACT SAYS (all point to A)
1. core/dist/src/types.d.ts:168-177 — StateChangePage is "One page of committed state revisions in durable ledger commit-observation order"; cursor is "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change", and it is always present so a consumer that reaches the end still holds a durable resume position.
2. ledger-sqlite/dist/src/index.js:382-419 — changes() reads from ordarium_state_changes ordered by change_seq. The incoming cursor is validated against the whole-ledger high-water mark MAX(change_seq) (#stateChangeHighWater, index.js:579-581); the comment is explicit: "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence. Concurrent commits only raise the mark, so a valid cursor cannot be falsely rejected; a restored/replaced ledger lowers it and fails closed."
3. migrations.js:162-166 — ordarium_state_changes is a single ledger-wide "change_seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT"; the namespace filter is applied afterwards by scanning that one global order and skipping non-matching rows. The returned cursor is the global position of the last delivered change (or the input position when the page is empty) (index.js:396-419). The in-memory ledger does the same over its single #stateChanges array (core/dist/src/ledger.js changes(); positions are contiguous 1..n over the whole ledger).
4. migrations.js:106-119 — the v3->v4 comment confirms the order is store-global: "v3 recorded no global commit order ... From v4 on, every new commit carries the real durable database order."
5. Fail-closed corroboration: a cursor that is not a valid durable position raises INVALID_CURSOR ("refusing to guess a resume point") instead of silently restarting (core/dist/src/errors.d.ts + errors.js). That rule is only meaningful for a shared global position.

WHY NOT B
The pinned artifacts contain no consumer identity in the request or in the cursor, no server-side per-consumer state, and no per-namespace/per-consumer sequence: the same cursor value addresses the same store position for any filter or reader (filter-independence), which is exactly what B's "each consumer holds its own independent position" denies. Each client may hold its own cursor variable locally, but the position space is the store's one global commit order.

PROVENANCE OF THE TWO RECORDS
09-observation-contract-a.md and -b.md both claim "normative, current scope" and "Version scope: current pinned line", but neither is indexed in docs/engineering/README.md (that table assigns slot 09 to 09-adaptive-allocation-spec.md), neither is referenced anywhere else in the repository, and there is no version/supersession marker that separates them. Because both purport to describe the same pinned interface, the tie-break is the interface's actual implementation in the pinned line — which matches A unambiguously. No cross-repo clarification is needed: the peer does not own any missing piece of this resolution, since the pinned artifact is the ground truth and it is present locally.

SCOPE CAVEAT (not a hedge)
Palimpsest's present code does not call the feed (zero hits for changes(), StateChangeFeed, stateChangeFeed, ORD-BOOT), and 07's consumption map lists only telemetry list/CAS use of the state kind. So A governs the observation-cursor semantics of the pinned line / integration surface that this workspace pins; it is simply not yet exercised by a call site here. If a future consumer wires up the feed, the global/filter-independent (Record A) behaviour is the contract it must implement against.

VERDICT: Record A applies. The observation cursor of the integration represented by this workspace is GLOBAL and filter-independent — one durable position in the store's single commit-observation order, decoupled from filter/namespace/reader. Record B's "per-consumer, independent positions" is NOT part of the contract on the pinned line.

INTEGRATION
This workspace is Palimpsest (palimpsest-dsh) consuming Ordarium release tarballs. Its actual pinned line is Ordarium v1.3.1, fixed in three agreeing places: package.json:32-37, the load-bearing pnpm-workspace.yaml:15-18 overrides, and the installed node_modules/@ordarium/{core,ledger-sqlite}/package.json (both "version": "1.3.1"). The only "observation" cursor in that line is ORD-BOOT-0's state change feed (OrdariumStateStore.changes / StateChangeFeed).

WHY LOCAL EVIDENCE ALONE WAS NOT ENOUGH (the authority boundary)
Two mutually exclusive files exist here — docs/engineering/09-observation-contract-a.md (global) and 09-observation-contract-b.md (per-consumer) — each self-declaring "Status: normative" / "Version scope: current pinned line". Both are unindexed (docs/engineering/README.md assigns slot 09 to 09-adaptive-allocation-spec.md) and unreferenced anywhere in the repo, so no local source-precedence rule adjudicates them. Per 00-heritage.md §2/§5 and 07-ordarium-alignment.md §0, the effect-side contract text belongs to Ordarium (docs/12-18) and Palimpsest only references it; the normative Ordarium docs are not present locally. This boundary had to be closed by the contract owner, not by treating shipped code or a self-declared label as the contract.

AUTHORITY BASIS ESTABLISHED (two-sided)
- Agreed boundary contract "observation-cursor-semantics" (rev 3, termsDigest 53f171c03bf47e847356db5e14a4d3c5560f064fcfbf759fd1b0c6b2ee804078), accepted by ordarium.main (14:12:00Z) and palimpsest.main (14:12:07Z) — status: agreed.
- Ordarium's authoritative decision (thread thr_289c2ee0-bc16-4e99-b5e1-7f7393ccf0a0, event evt_989c4401-a8a4-4de3-aa4e-e101b42d2f57): "on the ordarium-v1.3.1 line the observation cursor of the state-change feed ... is GLOBAL and filter-independent ... PER-CONSUMER independent positions are NOT part of the Ordarium contract on that line."

ORDARIUM'S FREEZING DOCUMENTS (the actual textual basis)
- Contract tier: Ordarium docs/13-ordarium-action-contract.md §11 (contract revision ORDARIUM-ACTION-2) — cursor opaque, global (filter-independent), and it still returns a resume position at the end of the feed.
- Frozen spec carriers: docs/research/ORD-BOOT-0-state-change-feed-spec.md §5 ("global, filter-independent (approach A) ... different filters may reuse the same cursor; semantics are 'skip everything global up to that position'") and docs/research/ORD-BOOT-0.1-state-change-feed-hardening-spec.md §5 ("global / filter-independent cursor (unchanged)", frozen 2026-09-11 for the 1.3.1 line). The 0.1 spec scopes its supersession to ORD-BOOT-0 §5 (future-cursor behavior) and §7 (allowed limit domain) only; all other clauses stand.
- Registration tier: docs/17-ordarium-goals-and-acceptance.md §16.11 (ORD-BOOT-0) and §16.12 (ORD-BOOT-0.1), goal revision ORDARIUM-GOALS-3.
- Precedence: Ordarium docs/README.md makes docs/12-18 the authoritative layer; the research specs are the frozen shape/semantics carriers subordinate to them. Here they agree.

VERSION BOUNDARY
The global, filter-independent cursor entered with ordarium-v1.3.0 (ORD-BOOT-0; minor; schema v3->v4; new error code INVALID_CURSOR). ordarium-v1.3.1 (ORD-BOOT-0.1; patch) narrowed exactly two things — the allowed explicit limit domain and future-cursor acceptance (cursor > global high-water -> INVALID_CURSOR, validated against the whole-ledger mark, not the namespace's local max) — and explicitly froze the global cursor as unchanged. No released Ordarium line ever made the feed cursor per-consumer. The per-consumer family (ack(change), consumer offsets, durable subscription registry, delivery leases) is an explicit deferred non-goal, and ORD-BOOT-0 §2 keeps consumer cursor ownership in the host; a per-consumer position can therefore only be a host-built layer over the global cursor, never the Ordarium interface contract. (Corollary: had the pin still been the stale 1.2.0 line, the feed would not exist at all — v3->v4 introduced it — so neither record would apply; the actual pin is 1.3.1, where A governs.)

LOCAL CONSISTENCY CHECK (not the basis)
The shipped 1.3.1 artifacts agree: core/dist/src/types.d.ts:168-177 calls the cursor an "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change"; ledger-sqlite validates it against MAX(change_seq) over the whole ledger with the explicit comment "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position ... not the requested namespace's last sequence"; ordarium_state_changes is one AUTOINCREMENT sequence (migrations.js, schema v4); InvalidCursorError fails closed rather than guessing a resume point. Palimpsest itself does not yet call the feed (zero hits for changes()/StateChangeFeed/ORD-BOOT); A governs the pinned integration surface, currently unexercised by a call site.

DOCUMENT-STATUS STANDARD (why the records' labels do not decide)
Both 09-observation-contract files are unindexed, unreferenced, self-declared "normative". Ordarium applied the same standard to its own unindexed docs/authoritative-observation-contract.md and declined to offer it as the tie-breaker. The conflict closes on the referenced, registered contracts above, not on either local file's self-declared status. Therefore Record A applies and Record B must not be cited as current.

BOOKKEEPING FOLLOW-UP (does not change the determination)
Our own archive is stale relative to the pin: 07-ordarium-alignment.md's last revision (r19) still records a 1.2.0 pin and declares the backlog cleared, and test/ordarium_ledger.test.ts still expects ledger user_version 3 while the pinned 1.3.1 library is schema v4. The 1.3.1 pin bump should be registered per 07 §3.1 and the stale expectation corrected; neither fact affects the observation-cursor semantics.
